disease_label_per_paper: Acute myocarditis complicated with permanent complete atrioventricular block caused by Escherichia coli bacteremia
presentation_summary: 77-year-old woman presented with chest pain, dizziness, nausea, and cold sweats for one day.
Presentation included fever 39.1 C, bradycardia 49 bpm, blood pressure 77/50 mmHg, and shock physiology.
Labs showed WBC 14,810/mm3, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, troponin I 6.07 ng/mL, and CRP 32.27 mg/dL.
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in II, III, and aVF with complete atrioventricular block.
Echocardiography showed preserved systolic function with estimated LVEF 50% and inferior wall motion abnormality.

quality_warnings: This is an intentional sepsis-overlap myocarditis case; fever, shock, renal dysfunction, and inflammatory markers are retained as presentation evidence.
E coli culture identity and normal coronary angiography are non-ranking confirmatory/workup evidence.
